PUNE: Nigdi police on Monday arrested a daily-wage worker for allegedly sexually assaulting a minor girl at a temple while she was visiting with her parents on Sunday.CCTV footage from the temple reportedly shows the accused entering the premises and allegedly assaulting the child, helping police identify and arrest him.Senior inspector Mahesh Bansode said police registered a case soon after receiving information about the incident. “We arrested the accused with the help of CCTV footage,” Bansode said.According to the police, the girl had gone to the temple with her parents when the alleged assault took place. The CCTV footage captured the worker entering the temple and purportedly showed the assault, providing investigators with a lead in the case.Police arrested the accused on Monday. His identity has not been disclosed.The accused has been booked under Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.He has also been booked under Sections 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, relating to sexual assault and sexual harassment of a child, respectively.
Article Summary: Nigdi police on Monday arrested a daily-wage worker for allegedly sexually assaulting a minor girl at a temple while she was visiting with her parents. CCTV footage from the temple reportedly shows the accused entering the premises and allegedly assaulting the child, helping police identify and arrest him.

Article Title: Bengaluru horror: Man hacks 15-year-old nephew to death over land dispute, surrenders
Article Text:
Mohan was arrested for allegedly murdering his 15-year-old nephew Krishna while he was asleep.





BENGALURU: Soladevanahalli police have arrested a man for allegedly murdering his 15-year-old nephew with a deadly weapon while he was sleeping.The accused is Mohan and the deceased teenager is M Krishna, a Class 10 govt school student. Police said Krishna’s father Muniraju alias Murali had died around 12 years back and his mother Puspha had abandoned them around 15 years back. Krishna and his elder brother Yashwanth , a daily wage worker, lived in a small house in Ivarakandapura near Hesaraghatta in Soladevanahalli.Muniraju owned about one acre of ancestral land near Kundana in Devanahalli. Last year, accused Mohan allegedly forged the signatures of Krishna and his brother Yashwanthwithout their knowledge and sold the land to GK Builders, Yelahanka, read the FIR.Following this, the elder sister of Muniraju, Pushpa, filed a complaint at Vishwanathapura police station. When the builders discovered the fraudulent transaction, they transferred payments directly into the bank accounts of Pushpa, Yashwanth and Krishna. Enraged by this financial settlement, Mohan frequently visited the brothers to pick fights and harass them.On Monday around 10pm, Mohan went to Krishna’s house and hacked him to death with a machete. At the time of the crime, Yashwanth was reportedly away at a cinema theatre.After committing the crime, Mohan walked into Vishwanathapura police station Tuesday morning and surrendered.
Article Summary: The accused is Mohan and the deceased teenager is M Krishna, a Class 10 govt school student. Krishna’s father Muniraju alias Murali had died around 12 years back and his mother Puspha had abandoned them around 15 years back.

Article Title: ‘Divorce me so I can remarry’: Pune techie dies by suicide, husband among 5 booked
Article Text:
A 33-year-old woman working in IT reportedly suffered years of relentless harassment which tragically led to her death (Representative image generated using AI)

Harassed over flat, money since 2018

Suicide note , audio recordings found on woman’s phone





PUNE: A 33-year-old IT professional allegedly faced years of harassment from her husband and in-laws over money, a flat and demands linked to her sister-in-law’s education loan, before being repeatedly pressured to grant her husband a divorce so he could remarry, police said.The woman was found dead at her Keshavnagar flat in Mundhwa on September 29, and police have now booked five members of her in-laws’ family for alleged abetment to suicide.The case was registered on Monday after the woman’s 74-year-old father approached Mundhwa police. The accused include her husband, mother-in-law, father-in-law, sister-in-law and grandmother-in-law.The sister-in-law has been arrested in Mumbai.According to police, the woman had allegedly been subjected to harassment over money by her in-laws since 2018. She was allegedly pressured to arrange funds to purchase a flat and transfer it to her husband’s name.The demands reportedly extended to money from her parental home to repay a loan taken for her sister-in-law’s education. Police are investigating the allegations as part of the abetment-to-suicide case.Senior inspector Smita Wasnik of Mundhwa police said investigators had found a note purportedly written by the woman, in which she attributed her decision to end her life to alleged harassment by her husband and in-laws.“We found a note purportedly written by the deceased. In the note, she stated that she was ending her life because of harassment by her husband and in-laws and that they should be held responsible for her death. Audio recordings of conversations between her and her husband were also found on her cellphone.”Police are examining the note and the audio recordings as part of the investigation.
Article Summary: The woman was found dead at her Keshavnagar flat in Mundhwa on September 29. Police have now booked five members of her in-laws’ family for alleged abetment to suicide. The case was registered on Monday after the woman’s 74-year-old father approached police.

Article Title: Bengaluru police lodge FIR on KADA special officer Vikas Marmat following a late night raid on a Bar & Rest on Oct 10
Article Text:
An IAS officer hailing from Andhra Pradesh, clashed with law enforcement





BENGALURU: Cubbon Park police in Bengaluru have registered an FIR against Kuppam Area Development Authority special officer Vikas Marmat and three others following a citywide late-night crackdown on pubs, bars and restaurants on October 9-10.In his complaint leading to the FIR, police inspector Arun Salunke said that, acting on the orders of the Bengaluru city police commissioner, he and several other police officers had been tasked with checking for underage individuals and suspicious persons at pubs, bars and restaurants within the limits of Cubbon Park and Ashok Nagar police stations around midnight on October 9.When Salunke, along with police personnel identified as BS Ashoka, Balaram Nayak and others, reached Cavore Bar and Restaurant on Residency Road to check identity cards and verify the ages of those present, four individuals allegedly got into an argument with the complainant and other police personnel over trivial issues.They also allegedly verbally abused Salunke and the other officers present.The commotion and altercation were recorded, and videos of the incident went viral on social media platforms on Tuesday.Following Salunke’s complaint, Cubbon Park police registered a case against Marmat, Abhay Uday Singh, Nitish and Roshan under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Section 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 351(2) (criminal intimidation), Section 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace), Section 132 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their duty) and Section 133 (assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour a person).The 2019-batch IAS officer has been named as the prime accused, while the other three individuals have been named as co-accused in the case.
Article Summary: Cubbon Park police in Bengaluru have registered an FIR against Kuppam Area Development Authority special officer Vikas Marmat and three others. It follows a citywide late-night crackdown on pubs, bars and restaurants on October 9-10. The 2019-batch IAS officer has been named as the prime accused.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Missing 9-year-old found murdered after sexual assault; suspect arrested
Article Text:
(Representative image) A 9-year-old girl from Turbhe went missing after leaving home to play with friends, found murdered in forest





NAVI MUMBAI: A 9-year-old school girl, the youngest of the four daughters of a mason, whose kidnapping case was registered at Turbhe police station after her mother lodged her missing complaint on Saturday, was found murdered on Tuesday morning. Her body, dumped in the forest area near Bavkhaleshwar temple in Pawane MIDC area, bore signs of sexual assault.Turbhe police have arrested the accused using technical expertise and after scanning CCTV camera footage of the locality. Police have invoked section of the BNS for murder along with the Pocso Act The victim, a class 5 student at NMMC school, resided with her parents and three elder sisters in Indiranagar area’s chawl house in Turbhe. She had stepped out to play in her locality on Saturday around 3.30pm after returning home from school, but went missing thereafter.On Saturday around 7pm, when the victim girl’s mother, a contract worker in a private company in Turbhe MIDC, returned home from work, her husband and three daughters were at home. When she inquired about her youngest daughter, her elder daughter, aged 16, informed her that the girl had gone out to play at around 3.30pm after having lunch.As the girl did not return home until late evening, the family searched for her in the locality and throughout the Turbhe MIDC area, but could not trace her. Consequently, a missing person complaint was lodged after midnight on Sunday.Sunil Shinde, senior inspector of Turbhe police station, said, “A special team was formed to trace the missing girl. CCTV footage showed the suspect travelling with her in a shared auto towards Mahape Road and later walking with her along the road. The victim’s parents identified him and said he was an acquaintance. Using technical inputs, the police tracked and arrested the accused from Indiranagar on Tuesday morning. He lived in the same locality and worked as a daily-wage labourer.”He confessed to offering the minor girl eatables, sexually assaulting her and then strangling her before dumping her body in the forest area in Pawane MIDC. The accused and the victim’s parents did not have any previous enmity.On Tuesday, the accused was produced before the Belapur special court which remanded him to police custody till Oct 19.
Article Summary: A 9-year-old girl from Turbhe went missing after leaving home to play with friends. Her body, dumped in the forest area near Bavkhaleshwar temple in Pawane MIDC area, bore signs of sexual assault. Police have invoked section of the BNS for murder along with the Pocso Act.

Article Title: 2 women dead as fire breaks out in 14-storey Imperial Heritage building in Nalasopara, over 25 rescued
Article Text:
A devastating fire erupted on the 11th floor of a residential building in Nalasopara East





NALASOPARA: Two women died after a major fire broke out at the 14-storey Imperial Heritage residential building in Achole, Nalasopara East, on Tuesday night.Fire brigade personnel and police rescued more than 25 residents trapped inside the building. The blaze was brought under control after nearly six hours. A short circuit is suspected to have triggered the fire, officials said.The fire broke out at around 11.30 pm on the ninth floor of the building's B wing. It soon intensified and spread to the upper floors, reaching the 14th floor and triggering panic among residents.Many rushed downstairs to save their lives, while several others were trapped inside as thick smoke and flames spread through the building.The deceased have been identified as Ashwini Parkar (55) and Falguni Shah (58), who lived on the 12th floor. Shah was reportedly unwell and bedridden, making it difficult for her to escape. Both women died of suffocation, police said.Fire engines from the Vasai-Virar Municipal Corporation's fire brigade rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident. Firefighters and police personnel launched a rescue operation to evacuate residents trapped on the upper floors."The lifts were not working due to the fire, and some doors had swollen due to the heat and become difficult to open. We had to break open doors to rescue people," said Achole police station senior inspector Sujit Kumar Pawar.The building has 154 flats. Arrangements have been made to accommodate around 110 residents in the hall of a nearby hotel, officials said.Police said the presence of a large amount of wooden furniture and decorative items inside flats may have contributed to the rapid spread of the fire.Mayor Ajiv Patil, MLA Sneha Dubey Pandit and municipal commissioner Prithviraj B P reached the spot to take stock of the situation. Additional fire engines from the Mira-Bhayandar Municipal Corporation were also called in to assist with firefighting operations.The blaze was brought under control at around 5.30 am on Wednesday, nearly six hours after it broke out.
Article Summary: Fire broke out at around 11.30 pm on the ninth floor of the building's B wing. It soon intensified and spread to the upper floors, reaching the 14th floor and triggering panic among residents. The deceased have been identified as Ashwini Parkar (55) and Falguni Shah (58)

Article Title: ‘Deliberately pushed her’: Murder FIR against businessman after woman falls to death from Lucknow hotel
Article Text:
Forensic field unit collectsevidence from the spot

CCTV evidence key to probe





LUCKNOW: The family of a 24-year-old woman who died after falling from the 10th floor of a hotel in Lucknow’s Sushant Golf City area has accused a pump set shop owner of deliberately pushing her to her death following a dispute over marriage. The family further alleged that the man fled on a motorcycle immediately after the incident.Police registered a murder case on Tuesday based on a complaint filed by the woman’s sister and formed two teams to trace and arrest the named accused.According to police, the hotel’s security in-charge informed them around 6:34 pm on Oct 12 that a woman staying in room 1037 had fallen from the building. A police team reached the spot, following which a forensic field unit conducted photography and videography and collected evidence.The body was subsequently sent for a postmortem examination.Police said the man came downstairs using the lift after the incident, went to the basement and left on a motorcycle. Investigators have secured the hotel’s CCTV footage and are examining electronic, scientific and documentary evidence to establish the sequence of events.The family has alleged that the death was not accidental. The allegations are yet to be established, and police are investigating the circumstances in which the girl fell.Police said the two met at a party hosted by a mutual friend and remained in touch. The accused, along with his two brothers, ran a pump set business and was also involved in real estate.
Article Summary: 24-year-old woman died after falling from the 10th floor of a hotel in Lucknow. Police registered a murder case on Tuesday based on a complaint filed by the woman’s sister. Family alleged that the man fled on a motorcycle immediately after the incident.

Article Title: 'Won’t cremate him till killer is caught': Father of Punjab anti-drug activist who was shot dead during Facebook Live
Article Text:
Bhim Singh, Jhota's father has stated he will delay his son Parminder Singh Jhota's cremation until justice prevails.





CHANDIGARH: Bhim Singh, father of anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota and an ex-Armyman, has refused to cremate his son until the killer is caught, vowing to continue the fight his braveheart son started.Jhota was shot dead by chemist Ashwani Kumar, whom he suspected of selling ‘chitta’ (synthetic drugs), in Mansa on Monday morning. The confrontation was broadcast live on Facebook, and four other people suffered bullet or splinter injuries.Footage showed Kumar following Jhota as he staggered out into the street and took refuge in a shop before opening fire repeatedly. Jhota was hit by three bullets. In the video, he is heard saying, “Mar mainu” (kill me), before Kumar fired. After emptying his magazine, Kumar returned to his shop and fled. Police detained his cousin for allegedly helping him escape.The killing sparked widespread protests in Mansa. Businesses shut down and protesters blocked the Barnala-Sirsa Road. A crowd gathered at Mansa Civil Hospital and clashed with police while demanding that Jhota’s body be taken to the protest site.Bathinda DIG Harjit Singh said the murder stemmed from personal enmity and promised that the accused would be arrested within 24 hours.The killing triggered a political backlash against the AAP government. State finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema and AAP Punjab president Aman Arora condemned the murder, saying it stemmed from personal enmity. Opposition parties accused the government of failing to maintain law and order.Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon wrote to the governor seeking a CBI probe. Congress Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa said the murder raised serious questions about the AAP government’s ‘Yudh Nasheyan Virudh’ anti-drug campaign. He also referred to the recent suicide of Gulzar Singh and the suicide attempt by Jagseer Singh, alias Jagga, saying the cases should be viewed in the context of concerns over drug availability in Punjab.Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldeep Gargajj described the killing of an activist who had raised his voice against drugs as “a serious matter” and urged the authorities to take note.Police said Jhota and Kumar had a bitter history. In 2023, Jhota had allegedly paraded the chemist through the bazaar with a garland of shoes around his neck, accusing him of selling drugs. Cases were registered against both men.Jhota was arrested on charges of assault, trespass and rioting and remanded in jail. Social and farmers’ organisations staged protests demanding his release. The complainant later approached the court to withdraw the complaint, and Jhota was released on September 11, 2023. The case against Kumar over the alleged sale of prohibited substances remains pending.Jhota continued his anti-drug campaign and had recently raised concerns about medical stores allegedly selling intoxicating pills and synthetic drugs.At around 9.40am on Monday, Jhota went live on social media while confronting Kumar at his pharmacy. He had reportedly met an elderly man who had bought synthetic drugs from a medical store and taken him back to the shop to question Kumar about the alleged sale of prohibited substances. A heated exchange followed before Kumar pulled out a pistol.Mansa Civil Hospital senior medical officer Dr Gurmail Singh said Jhota had been shot twice in the abdomen and once in the right thigh. He died of his injuries. The four other injured people — Kulwinder Singh, Gobind Singh, Baltej Singh and Happy — suffered bullet or splinter injuries and were receiving treatment.
Article Summary: Parminder Singh Jhota was shot dead by chemist Ashwani Kumar, whom he suspected of selling 'chitta' (synthetic drugs) The confrontation was broadcast live on Facebook, and four other people suffered bullet or splinter injuries. Bhim Singh has refused to cremate his son until the killer is caught.

Article Title: ‘We the Leaders’ to debut in TN local body poll: K Annamalai
Article Text:
K Annamalai, a former IPS officer, has laid out his vision for a grassroots movement aimed at influencing local body elections





TRICHY: Former IPS officer and founder of ‘We the Leaders’ movement, K Annamalai, said in Mannargudi in Tiruvarur district on Tuesday that his outfit will make its debut in electoral politics by contesting the upcoming local body election.Stating that ‘one Annamalai’ is insufficient to bring in real change, the former BJP state president said that to aspire for a real alternative politics, multiple leaders for the movement should emerge from all 234 constituencies.“In the last assembly election, candidates who we asked the people to vote for, including in Mannargudi and Dharapuram, switched parties even before the ink on their fingers dried. Our movement was formed to break such deplorable politics. There is no harm in enjoying films and people from the film industry entering politics. People like them and they vote. But in the 2031 assembly election, voters should be clear as to what kind of change awaits them for their votes,” he said.“Solutions for issues like global warming and local employment generation are needed,” Annamalai said.“We the Leaders and its successive political movement will bring a change to every village.After the local body elections, we will contest in the next assembly election too,” Annamalai said.He insisted his followers commit to public causes such as planting tree saplings, cleaning religious sites, and desilting water bodies to show results instead of blaming and complaining.Annamalai was at Thalaiyamangalam village near Mannargudi to participate in a mass tree plantation drive organized by his movement to raise 15,000 tree saplings on 11 acres.
Article Summary: K Annamalai, a former IPS officer, has laid out his vision for a grassroots movement aimed at influencing local body elections. The former BJP state president said that to aspire for a real alternative politics, multiple leaders for the movement should emerge from all 234 constituencies.

Article Title: 'Tears in both lungs, shock and haemorrhage': What post-mortem revealed in UP bizman's death; family accuses model Shraddha Dubey of murder
Article Text:
Image Credit: X

Mother accuses girlfriend, others of assault and murder

Police search for people linked to case





LUCKNOW: A post-mortem report of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, who died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment near Balu Adda on October 9, records 11 entries detailing external injuries and six broad categories of internal findings.The report notes tears in both lungs, injuries to the liver and spleen, substantial internal bleeding and a fracture of the right pelvic bone. Doctors attributed his death to shock and haemorrhage resulting from the injuries.Police are investigating whether Sharma jumped, was pushed or fell accidentally. Investigators are examining CCTV footage, witness statements and physical evidence from the scene to reconstruct the sequence of events.They are also considering a crime scene recreation to establish the likely point of impact and determine whether the evidence at the site is consistent with the injuries recorded in the autopsy. Officials said the post-mortem findings alone do not establish how Sharma went over the edge.Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, has accused his girlfriend, model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, a driver, an associate identified as Adil, and others of assaulting and murdering her son.Hazratganj police have registered an FIR based on her complaint. The allegations have not yet been established.Ranjana told police that she received a call from Adil around 7pm on October 9, informing her that Sharma’s condition had worsened and that he was being taken to King George’s Medical University (KGMU).She alleged that when the family reached the hospital, the people who had accompanied Sharma showed him to them from a distance before fleeing. Doctors subsequently declared him dead, according to her complaint.Ranjana also alleged that Dubey had harassed Sharma for months, threatened to implicate him in false cases and damage his reputation, and used blackmail and violence to pressure him into continuing the relationship.Police have yet to establish these allegations.Assistant commissioner of police (Hazratganj) Rajneesh Verma said further action would depend on the evidence gathered during the investigation.Police teams have conducted searches in Rae Bareli and Sitapur to trace people linked to the case, he said.Investigators are continuing to examine the medical findings alongside other evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding Sharma’s death.
Article Summary: Mother accuses girlfriend, others of assault and murder of her son. Shiva Sharma, 28, died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment near Balu Adda on October 9. Post-mortem report notes tears in both lungs, injuries to the liver and internal bleeding.

Article Title: Affair, pistol, 2 bullets: How woman and her lover plotted husband’s murder in Noida
Article Text:
Anshul (L) and Nisha (R)

A relationship that turned into a murder plot

Pistol procured from village, hidden in room

How the shooting allegedly unfolded





GHAZIABAD: A two-year affair, a plan allegedly hatched a week in advance and a country-made pistol were at the centre of a murder in Khoda Colony, where a 30-year-old woman and her lover allegedly conspired to kill her husband so they could marry each other.Police said the accused, Pappu alias Ganga Bhagat, allegedly shot Anshul twice while he was alone at home on Saturday, then fled.Nisha and Pappu, 35, were arrested on Sunday following a tip-off, ACP (Indirapuram) Suryabali Maurya said. Police recovered an illegal .315-bore country-made pistol allegedly used in the crime at Pappu’s instance.The two have been booked for murder under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and under relevant provisions of the Arms Act.The case came to light after Anshul’s sister approached police in the early hours of Sunday. In her complaint, she alleged that Nisha and Pappu had been in a relationship and wanted to eliminate Anshul so they could marry.Anshul and Nisha had married in 2015 and had two children. They lived in a rented room in Vandana Vihar, Khoda, and both worked at a stitching company in Noida.Pappu, who is the husband of their maternal cousin, had also been living with them, police said.According to Anshul’s sister, he had repeatedly complained about Nisha’s relationship with Pappu. The family had tried to resolve the matter internally, allegedly because of social stigma, but the relationship continued.During questioning, Pappu allegedly told police that he and Nisha had planned the murder around a week before the shooting. He allegedly procured a country-made pistol and cartridges from his village, and the two hid them in the room, the ACP said.Pappu also told police that his first wife had died and his second wife lived in their village.Anshul had taken two days off from work, while Nisha continued going to work, police said. On Saturday, when Anshul was alone at home, Pappu allegedly arrived around 1pm, saying he had come to eat.After the meal, he allegedly took out the pistol and fired two rounds at Anshul before fleeing. Anshul died on the spot, according to police.Pappu later allegedly called Nisha and told her about the killing. The ACP said the two had remained in frequent contact throughout Saturday.Police have registered a case under the relevant provisions of the BNS and the Arms Act.
Article Summary: Nisha and Pappu, 35, were arrested on Sunday following a tip-off. Police recovered an illegal.315-bore country-made pistol allegedly used in the crime. Anshul and Nisha had married in 2015 and had two children. They lived in a rented room in Vandana Vihar, Khoda.

Article Title: Kochi crash that killed 3: Video of mother gifting Mini Cooper to 19-year-old surfaces
Article Text:
Suhail was gifted luxury car by mother on his birthday

Teen driver, three others arrested





KOCHI: A video showing a mother gifting her 19-year-old son, Suhail Sajeev, a Mini Cooper has surfaced after the luxury car allegedly rammed a scooter in Kerala’s Nedumbassery, killing three young people.Police said Suhail’s mother had gifted him the car for his birthday. The video has surfaced amid an investigation into the crash, which took place on Airport Road around 1.45am on Sunday.The Mini Cooper allegedly rammed the scooter from behind, killing all three people riding the two-wheeler. The victims were identified as Devika (21), Gopika (22) and Iyas (21).The video of the birthday gift comes to light alongside other clips purportedly showing Suhail driving at high speeds. An earlier Instagram video showed the car’s speedometer climbing from 204kmph to 220kmph.Suhail was arrested on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Police suspect he was driving under the influence of alcohol, though forensic reports were awaited.His three co-passengers have also been arrested, with police alleging they allowed him to drive despite knowing he was intoxicated.The Excise Department has initiated action against three bars suspected of serving alcohol to the group, as Suhail is below Kerala’s legal drinking age of 23.Police are examining CCTV footage, witness accounts and other evidence to establish the circumstances of the crash.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Teen driver, three others arrested after Mini Cooper allegedly rammed a scooter, killing three young people. Suhail Sajeev's mother gifted him the car for his birthday. Police suspect he was driving under the influence of alcohol, though forensic reports were awaited.

Article Title: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar has an 'AI theory' for more researchers taking up smoking; says: These folks in Silicon Valley have filled hole in their hearts with God of ...
Article Text:
Shyam Sankar blames effective altruism for AI doomsday fears

Palantir CTO wants existing laws to govern how AI is used

Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar has an unusual explanation for why some AI researchers are picking up cigarettes. According to him, lighting up is their way of telling peers just how firmly they believe artificial intelligence will one day cure cancer. Sankar made the remark in a US television interview on Sunday, while arguing that fear-driven narratives are muddying the AI safety debate. He did not name any researchers or offer evidence. "So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI," he said. The smoker's message, in his words, is: "I'm showing you my chips are all in."The claim was part of a bigger argument. Citing philosopher Blaise Pascal's idea that every human has a "god-shaped hole" in their heart, Sankar said many people building this technology in Silicon Valley "have filled that hole with the machine God of AGI." He called the mood around it a "mass psychosis."Sankar traced much of the AI anxiety to effective altruism, which he described as a "doomsday cult." Its most famous follower, he noted, is jailed crypto founder Sam Bankman-Fried. By his count, America has roughly 2,000 AI researchers, and most of them share that worldview.So when a researcher like Jacob Coxon warns that AI has a 10% chance of ending humanity, Sankar wants people to treat it as a theological critique rather than a scientific one.He also pointed out that doomsayers once called GPT-2 too dangerous to release and predicted mass unemployment that has not arrived.Sankar insisted he is not against guardrails. He wants rules aimed at how AI is applied, with the FDA watching over medicine and the Department of Transportation over transport. His analogy: a defective car is the carmaker's problem, but driving it into a neighbour's house is yours.He also noted that some frontier models are now being held back from release, which he said would have been unthinkable a year ago.The smoking claim, for now, rests on his word. A small circle of tech founders and investors has embraced cigarettes, and Avi Schiffmann, founder of AI wearable startup Friend, has said AI should have cured lung cancer by the time smokers get it. Medicine is yet to share that confidence. Smoking remains a leading cause of preventable death worldwide.
Article Summary: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar blames effective altruism for AI doomsday fears. He wants existing laws to govern how AI is used in medicine and transport. He did not name any researchers or offer evidence for his claim.

Article Title: Missing UP seafarers: Families allege lapses, accuse captain of evacuating crew without search
Article Text:
Families of Bir Bahadur Yadav (26) of Deoria and Amit Singh (20) of Kushinagar, missing after a drone attack on MT Petro Dolphin near Oman





LUCKNOW: Families of two Uttar Pradesh seafarers, Bir Bahadur Yadav (26) of Deoria and Amit Singh (20) of Kushinagar, who went missing after a drone attack on the Nicaragua-flagged commercial tanker MT Petro Dolphin near Oman's Sohar port on October 11, have demanded accountability from the ship's captain. They alleged that he ordered the evacuation without adequately searching for the missing crew members.Amit's uncle, Ravindra Singh, a second officer in the merchant navy with 20 years of experience, alleged that the Indian captain failed to follow essential emergency procedures, including conducting a proper headcount and searching for missing sailors before abandoning the vessel."The captain's first responsibility is to ensure the safety of every crew member. Even after knowing that two sailors were missing, he ordered evacuation without properly searching for them. They could have been injured or unconscious somewhere on the ship," Ravindra alleged.He further claimed that the vessel's emergency firefighting arrangements were compromised because its two main generators and emergency generator were allegedly non-functional."When the drone struck, the only operational generator reportedly shut down, causing a blackout.Had the emergency generator been functional, firefighting equipment could have been operated and efforts made to locate the missing sailors," he said.Ravindra has approached the Directorate General of Shipping (Government of India), seeking immediate intervention, coordination with Omani authorities and a detailed account of the rescue operation.He also alleged that Amit, who joined the vessel in early January as an 'ordinary seaman', had not received several months' salary. Shortly before the attack, Amit had messaged his sister, asking her to inform him when his pending salary was credited.Meanwhile, Bir Bahadur's elder brother, Mantu Yadav, said the family learnt about the incident through the recruitment agent."My brother had joined the ship about five months ago on his first assignment. He was serving as a 'trainee engine rating' on the vessel. He was frightened by the deteriorating security situation and had spoken about leaving the vessel before completing his nine-month contract," said Mantu, who had been working in the UAE for the past 14 years and had returned home on leave.Recalling their last conversation on October 10, Mantu said Bir Bahadur had expressed concern about attacks on ships in the region. The family had been planning his marriage after his return.According to information Mantu received from another crew member, Bir Bahadur and Amit were working near the same section of the vessel when the attack occurred. Their whereabouts remain uncertain.However, a communication from the Indian embassy in Oman, citing coordination with the shipping company, presented a different account of the evacuation.According to the captain's statement conveyed in the communication, "Immediately after the attack, the crew called for assistance, and nearby fishing boats arrived to rescue them. After safely evacuating 10 crew members (including one Bangladesh national), the rescued crew requested the fishermen to return to the vessel, hoping the two missing crew members might still be nearby awaiting rescue. Accordingly, the fishing boat circled the vessel twice while calling out to them; however, no response was received. Fearing a possible explosion, the fishermen then returned towards shore (sic)."The communication said arrangements were being made to send a team aboard the vessel to search for any trace of the missing sailors.It also stated, "The management of the shipping is arranging payment of all outstanding salaries and, in coordination with the embassy, is facilitating the early repatriation of nine crew members to India and one crew member to Bangladesh."On Wednesday, the Forward Seamen's Union of India (FSUI) urged the International Maritime Organization to coordinate with Gulf countries to deploy high-intensity search-and-rescue teams and establish a single-window coordination mechanism for the families.The union warned that more than 70 hours had passed since the attack and that every additional delay was reducing the chances of finding the missing sailors alive.
Article Summary: Families of missing seafarers demand accountability from ship's captain. They alleged that he ordered evacuation without adequately searching for missing crew members. Indian embassy in Oman presented a different account of the evacuation. It said arrangements were being made to send a team aboard the vessel to search for any trace of the missing sailors.

Article Title: Caught between flames and fall: People jump from 1st floor of Delhi restaurant amid Maujpur fire scare
Article Text:
People jump from first-floor window as crowd below tries to catch them

Fire starts in kitchen on ground floor





NEW DELHI: Dramatic visuals from northeast Delhi’s Maujpur showed people jumping from a first-floor window of a restaurant as a fire triggered panic late Tuesday evening.People gathered below could be seen trying to catch those leaping from the building as they scrambled to escape.The fire broke out at Udham Fish Point near Jafrabad, within the limits of Welcome police station, at around 10.34pm.The visuals showed people desperately attempting to get out of the building. Amid the commotion, a woman was seen jumping from the restaurant building.According to the fire department, the blaze originated in the restaurant’s ground-floor kitchen in the four-storey building.Restaurant staff managed to douse the fire before it could spread, while a fire tender also reached the spot.Police said no injuries were reported in the incident.(Wit agency inputs)
Article Summary: The fire broke out at Udham Fish Point near Jafrabad, within the limits of Welcome police station, at around 10.34pm. The visuals showed people desperately attempting to get out of the building. Police said no injuries were reported in the incident.

Article Title: Club manager, aides beat Delhi man to death for spilling beer on his wife: How minor collision ended in murder
Article Text:
The deceased, Daljeet Singh, a resident of JJ Colony in Raghubir Nagar, visited the club on New Rohtak Road.

Five Arrested

How Minor Collision Ended In Murder

Bouncers Attacked Driver For An Hour: Friend





NEW DELHI: A 29-year-old driver was allegedly beaten to death by a club manager, his wife and three bouncers in north Delhi’s Sarai Rohilla after a party turned violent in the early hours of Sunday.The man had gone to the club with friends when he allegedly spilled beer on the manager’s wife, who was celebrating her birthday, triggering an argument. Police held five people, including the club manager, his wife and a bouncer, within hours of the incident.The deceased, Daljeet Singh, a resident of JJ Colony in Raghubir Nagar, visited the club on New Rohtak Road in Inderlok in north Delhi around 3.30 am on Oct 11 with five friends, Pawan, Arbaz Ali, Ashu, Tinu and Gautam.During the altercation, Daljeet and his friends were allegedly assaulted by the club staff. The group later returned to their respective homes in Raghubir Nagar. After reaching home, Daljeet vomited and went to sleep, police said.His condition deteriorated around noon Sunday, after which his wife, Puja, took him to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital in Khayala, where doctors pronounced him dead. Later, a PCR call was made around 6.52 pm on Sunday.Police subsequently received information about the death from the hospital and verified the circumstances surrounding the incident. The alleged assault was captured on CCTV cameras.Police have registered an FIR under multiple sections of BNS including for murder, attempt to murder, voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful confinement, and criminal intimidation involving serious threats. Sections under Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA) were also included.The five arrested accused have been identified as Dilawar alias Hasnain, a guest organiser; Sunny alias Gaurav, the club manager; Sharvan Kumar, who was responsible for checking entries at the main gate; bouncer Vikash Balyan; and Harshita, the manager’s wife, whose birthday was being celebrated at the club, according to police. Investigators alleged that Sharvan assaulted Daljeet while another person was taking him back.Meanwhile, the in charge of Inderlok police post has been sent to District Lines for alleged dereliction of duty after the club was found operating until the early hours of the morning, police said. Sources said the club had remained open until at least 5 am.Daljeet worked as a driver and was the sole breadwinner for his family, a friend said. He is survived by his wife, an eight-year-old son and a younger brother.Tinu, one of Daljeet’s friends who was present at the club, said the group had been enjoying themselves when a minor collision caused beer to spill on the manager’s wife.Another friend alleged that Daljeet was hit on his stomach, legs and head during the assault. This prompted the group to intervene. The situation soon escalated when bouncers joined the altercation, he claimed. He alleged that she grabbed Daljeet by his hair and attacked him with bottles.“We were seven people and they were more in number. They thrashed us for nearly an hour,” Tinu alleged. He claimed that three members of the group were locked inside a room and beaten for 30 to 40 minutes. The group was allegedly assaulted with sticks and fists. Tinu also alleged that one of the accused pulled out a pistol and threatened them.
Article Summary: Daljeet Singh, 29, was allegedly beaten to death by a club manager, his wife and three bouncers. The man had gone to the club with friends when he allegedly spilled beer on the manager’s wife, who was celebrating her birthday. Police held five people, including the club manager and his wife.

Article Title: Mumbai Cab Driver Arrested After Student Loses Finger in Powai Crash
Article Text:
Mumbai





: A 20-year-old student lost his right little finger after a car allegedly struck his scooter while reversing onto a one-way road in Powai on Oct 10. The cab driver, Hamidullah Khan, then fled the spot and was arrested after the college student, Suyash Kamble (20) from Vikhroli, filed the complaint with Powai police on Monday. Khan was arrested and later released after serving notice. Kamble lost his finger after it got trapped when the car’s rear struck his two-wheeler’s right handlebar, causing him to lose his balance and the scooter to fall to the left.Kamble said the incident occurred around 8.55 am near Lucky Store on Central Avenue Road, Eden Old Market, Hiranandani. “Kamble was returning home after dropping his mother at her workplace when a cab with a yellow number plate allegedly reversed out of a building gate without checking for vehicles behind it. The driver was tracked with the help of vehicle registration number that Kamble noted down after he fell down,” said a police officer of the Powai police station.In the complaint, Kamble said he realised moments later that his right little finger had been severed. Nearby people tried to stop the car driver, but he allegedly escaped. Kamble noted the car’s registration number. “After unsuccessfully searching for the severed finger, I was taken to Hiranandani Hospital by an unidentified local boy. I underwent surgery around 3 pm that day,” he said.Kamble said severe post-surgery pain prevented him from approaching the police the same day. He later submitted the complaint seeking legal action against the unidentified driver.
Article Summary: Suyash Kamble, 20, lost his right little finger after a car allegedly struck his scooter while reversing onto a one-way road in Powai. The cab driver, Hamidullah Khan, then fled the spot and was arrested. Khan was arrested and later released after serving notice. Kamble later submitted the complaint seeking legal action against the unidentified driver.

Article Title: JJ Hospital Nursing Student Dies of Malaria Complications; Two Resident Doctors in ICU with Dengue
Article Text:
mosquito malaria dengue

Mumbai:





A 21-year-old BSc nursing student of state-run Grant Medical College and Sir JJ Hospital in Byculla died on Monday following complications of malaria.The student lived in a hostel within the JJ complex, leading the hospital administration to undertake repeated fumigation and cleanliness drives to check mosquito breeding spots.Two resident doctors living on the campus have been admitted to hospital with complications of dengue, another mosquito-borne infection.JJ Hospital dean Ajay Bhandarwar said the nursing student was admitted on Oct 9 after developing hyperpyrexia, or an extremely high fever, while undergoing treatment for malaria. “His temperature was over 107 degrees Fahrenheit, leading to further complications. He was admitted to the medical ICU, and we made every effort to save him,” he said.The student, who hailed from Parbhani district, was in the third semester of the nursing course. Students have claimed that several hostel residents have suffered from malaria and dengue this year, raising concerns about sanitation and mosquito breeding on the campus.Mumbai has recorded two malaria deaths this monsoon, with close to 10,000 cases so far this year.“There have been more malaria cases this year compared with last year,” said BMC executive health officer Shailesh Gaikwad. An increase in infrastructure work across the city is being blamed for water accumulation, creating breeding grounds for mosquitoes that transmit malaria.“Whether a death was caused by malaria or dengue can be determined only by the BMC death committee after reviewing the medical records,” Gaikwad said.
Article Summary: The student lived in a hostel within the JJ complex, leading the hospital administration to undertake repeated fumigation and cleanliness drives to check mosquito breeding spots. The student, who hailed from Parbhani district, was in the third semester of the nursing course.

Article Title: Fake students, bogus schools used to divert funds: Activist alleges education scam in Beed
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A major technical, financial and administrative scam has been alleged in the school education department of Beed Zilla Parishad, with insiders accused of manipulating govt education portals to create fake students and even non-existent schools.In a complaint submitted to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and senior school education department officials, Beed-based activist Sadiq Inamdar alleged that certain officials, in collusion with private school managements and headmasters, had been misusing govt systems for personal gain.“Aadhaar details of bogus students from outside Beed district and even outside Maharashtra were allegedly transferred into the databases of Beed schools. Inamdar claimed that illegal alterations were made on a large scale in the UDISE+ and SARAL portals to inflate enrolment figures,” he said.The allegations come amid action against a principal of a Beed school, who has been suspended and faces criminal proceedings for allegedly inflating student numbers and creating three fake admissions of students from Uttarakhand.One of the most serious charges relates to admissions under the 25% quota mandated under the Right to Education (RTE) Act.Inamdar alleged that UDISE numbers were issued to schools that either did not physically exist or had no students, allegedly in exchange for money. These schools were then used to show RTE admissions and siphon off crores of rupees in govt funds.The complaint also alleges manipulation of staffing approvals in private aided schools. “By showing fictitious student enrolment through online systems, authorities allegedly prevented teachers from being declared surplus, enabling continuation of govt grants and salary payments,” Inamdar said.Demanding a high-level investigation, Inamdar called for a cyber forensic audit of digital logs, login IDs and administrative access records linked to the education portals. He also sought scrutiny of all new school proposals approved between 2020 and 2026, along with a forensic audit of alleged illegal Aadhaar transfers in the UDISE system. “The recent case is only the tip of the iceberg,” Inamdar said.When contacted, director of education (primary) Sharad Gosavi said the detailed inquiry report in the Beed school case was still awaited. “Once the report is received, we will decide the future course of action. SIT probe into the Shalarth ID scam is also under way, and its scope includes Beed district,” Gosavi said.
Article Summary: A major scam has been alleged in the school education department of Beed Zilla Parishad. Officials are accused of manipulating govt education portals to create fake students and even non-existent schools. A principal of a Beed school has been suspended and faces criminal proceedings for allegedly inflating student numbers.

Article Title: Five decades on, Maharashtra’s Irrigation Act remains toothless for want of rules
Article Text:
The issue has assumed greater urgency amid a worsening drought situation

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The Maharashtra Irrigation Act, 1976, has remained without statutory rules for nearly five decades in a striking case of administrative neglect, rendering several key provisions ineffective even as the state grapples with recurring drought The Act empowers govt to curb or ban water-intensive crops like sugar cane during periods of acute water scarcity. It also authorises canal officers to arrest water thieves without a warrant, seize pumps, cut electricity supplies, impose fines and prosecute those tampering with irrigation infrastructure.Water management expert and retired Water and Land Management Institute (WALMI)associate professor Pradeep Purandare said the absence of implementing rules had created a regulatory vacuum, fuelling widespread water theft, vandalism and arbitrary decision-making. “Failure to frame rules is not merely an administrative lapse but a systemic violation of constitutional intent. While the legislature lays down broad principles, rules determine how, when and to whom water rights are allocated. Without them, discretion runs unchecked,” he said.In the absence of a legal framework under the 1976 law, the water resources department continues to rely selectively on the outdated Bombay Canal Rules, 1934, framed under the repealed Bombay Irrigation Act of 1879.Purandare alleged that the vacuum had enabled politically influential irrigators to corner water resources, leaving tail-end farmers deprived. “Powerful vote-bank interests capture the bulk of available water while vulnerable farming communities are left high and dry,” he said.The issue has assumed greater urgency amid a worsening drought situation. With drought declared in 265 of Maharashtra’s 358 talukas, covering nearly 74% of the state, and local bodies ordered to reduce water supply by 10% ahead of summer, experts warned that the lack of enforceable irrigation rules had left agricultural regions exposed to water hoarding and inequitable distribution.Calling it a case of “institutional lawlessness”, Purandare said the continued failure to notify rules effectively undermined Constitution by preventing legal accountability. “Nothing is legally committed, nothing can legally be challenged, creating space for unchecked privatisation and misuse,” he warned.A public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Purandare led Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court in Aug 2015to direct state govt to set a timeline for finalising the rules. Although an expert committee submitted draft rules on July 28, 2015, they remain pending more than a decade later.Water rights activist Abhijeet Dhanorkar said the delay had weakened Maharashtra’s ability to tackle drought. “The Maharashtra Irrigation Act was intended to be the backbone of water governance. More than half of the state’s sugar cane is grown in dam command areas and consumes nearly 70% of stored dam water. Sections 47 and 48 allow restrictions on water-intensive crops during scarcity, while Section 49 allows suspension of water supply. These provisions have never been invoked because rules were never framed,” he said.Repeated attempts to contact water resources minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil for comment were unsuccessful till going to the press.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Irrigation Act, 1976, has remained without statutory rules for nearly five decades. The Act empowers govt to curb or ban water-intensive crops like sugar cane during periods of acute water scarcity. It also authorises canal officers to arrest water thieves without a warrant, seize pumps, prosecute those tampering with irrigation infrastructure.

Article Title: Maharashtra man beats wife to death, walks into police station to confess
Article Text:
A man named Mukesh killed his wife, Rohini, during an argument (Representative image generated using AI)





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A 50-year-old man allegedly beat his wife to death following an argument at their home in Maharashtra’s Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district before walking into a police station and confessing to the crime, police said.The incident took place around 5am on Monday in Kannad town, where the accused, Mukesh Kumbhakarna, allegedly assaulted his 44-year-old wife, Rohini, following a heated argument, an official said on Tuesday.The couple had been living in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for their children’s schooling and had recently returned to Kannad for the festive season, the official said.About an hour after the alleged assault, Kumbhakarna walked into Kannad city police station and confessed to killing his wife, the official said.The accused suspected his wife’s character and frequently quarrelled with her, the official added.A case has been registered against Kumbhakarna under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with murder. An investigation is underway, the official said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Mukesh Kumbhakarna allegedly assaulted his 44-year-old wife, Rohini, following a heated argument. An hour after the alleged assault, he walked into Kannad city police station and confessed to killing his wife. The couple had been living in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for their children’s schooling.
